summary: Round 2 closes the two critical implementation problems and most of the requested documentation/test follow-ups: the BB84 finite-key path now separates pre-EC entropy from EC leakage, the heuristic rename/disclosure for the former `kamin_theorem3_key_length` path landed, the new regression tests would catch the C1 double-count, and the PHASE1/GEAT/Kamin/TF literature notes include the requested errata. I did not find new security, performance, or runtime error-handling regressions in the patch. I could not run `pytest` in this read-only sandbox because the environment has no writable temp directory, so the review is based on static inspection plus direct numeric spot-checks. One major documentation-correctness issue remains in the PM-QKD formulation fix, so the patch is not ready for PASS.

issues.description: M1 is only partially fixed. After correctly introducing the phase register `R_A`, the new "Fock 对角化 on announcement" subsection still says that, after phase announcement, the conditional optical state `ρ_{A' | R_A = φ, K_A = κ}` "退化为 Poisson Fock 数混合". At fixed announced `φ`, that state is still the coherent state `|α e^{i(φ+πκ)}⟩`; the Poisson/Fock-diagonal mixture appears only after averaging or tracing over the phase register, not after conditioning on it. This is the central semantic point of the Round-1 M1 bug, so the revised text still risks guiding a downstream implementation to diagonalize the source too early.
issues.suggestion: Rewrite this subsection so the conditioned announced state stays coherent, and state separately that tracing out or averaging over the phase register yields the `κ`-independent Poisson mixture. Avoid wording that ties Fock diagonalization to the announced-phase conditional state.

issues.description: `bb84_qubit_finite_key_length()` now correctly brands the path as heuristic, but its docstring still says the Stage-1 shortcuts "underestimate the key length at small n". That is justified for the conservative `Var(f)=1` bound, but not for dropping the `inf_{p,J}` min-tradeoff optimization from Theorem 3, whose sign is not guaranteed. This wording reintroduces a weaker version of the old C2 overclaim.
issues.suggestion: Rephrase the closing sentence to say the heuristic differs from the full Theorem 3 result and that only the `Var(f)=1` part is known to be conservative; the net bias of omitting the min-tradeoff optimization is not established.

round_recommendation: Fix the PM-QKD phase-announcement/Fock-diagonalization explanation in `docs/msen/pm_qkd_formulation.md`, and tighten the remaining heuristic wording in `qkdx/finite_key/kamin_geat.py` so it does not imply a guaranteed conservative bias.
